In the Calvin cycle (C3 photosynthesis), the carbon in CO₂ is initially fixed to the five-carbon molecule ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) [d2][d10]. This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO, and the resulting six-carbon intermediate immediately splits to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate [d3][d4][d10]. In C4 photosynthesis, however, CO₂ is initially fixed to a different molecule: phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) in the mesophyll cells, forming the four-carbon compound oxaloacetic acid (OAA) [d8]. This C4 pathway is an addition to the ancestral C3 pathway, and the CO₂ is ultimately passed to RuBisCO in the bundle sheath cells for the standard Calvin cycle reactions [d8][d5].
